name: Café au lait
caffeine: From the brewed coffee, which is half the cup; the hot milk adds none.

house.ask: Not printed on our menus: ask at lineup whether the bar makes one from our chicory coffee and hot milk, and at what price.

what: French for coffee with milk: strong brewed coffee, not espresso, with an equal measure of milk heated until it steams. It carries little or no foam, so it is plain and soft rather than textured, and it needs no espresso machine. The New Orleans version, with chicory, has its own entry.
taste: Soft, round and mild: the roast comes through, gentled by the milk, with none of a latte's airy foam.

steps: Brew coffee strong, about 60 to 65 g per litre, by drip or press.
Heat an equal measure of milk until it steams, about 149F (65C); never boil it.
Pour the coffee and the milk into a warmed cup together, in equal parts.
Offer sugar on the side and serve at once.
make.ratio: Equal parts strong brewed coffee and hot milk
make.dose: 60 to 65 g coffee per litre; equal milk
make.time: Batch 4 to 8 minutes; sell within 30 to 60 minutes sealed
make.cup: Warmed cup or mug, 6 to 12 oz

serve: On a saucer with a teaspoon, sugar offered on the side. It is the milky coffee to suggest when no espresso drink is on offer, since it needs only brewed coffee.
story: The name is plain French, and the drink needs only a pot of coffee and a pan of milk. Guests confuse it with a latte: the difference is brewed coffee against espresso, milk heated against textured. In New Orleans the words mean chicory coffee and hot milk, so ask a visitor which.
guest: Brewed coffee with an equal measure of hot milk: softer and plainer than a latte, with almost no foam.
watch: Boiled milk gives a skin and a cooked taste; heat it only until it steams.
Coffee held on a hotplate goes flat; pour from a fresh pot or a sealed airpot.
Weak coffee makes a thin cup; brew at the strong end rather than cutting the milk.

recall.prompt: What is in a café au lait, and how is it made?
recall.answer: Strong brewed coffee, about 60 to 65 g per litre, with an equal measure of milk heated until it steams, about 149F (65C), poured together into a warmed cup. Soft, round, no foam.

quiz.q: What coffee is the base of a classic café au lait?
quiz.explain: Brewed coffee, drip or press, with hot milk; espresso under milk makes a latte or café con leche.

quiz.q: Why should café au lait milk never boil?
options: It whips into a stiff foam
quiz.explain: Boiled milk grows a skin and tastes cooked; heat it only until it steams, about 149F (65C).

quiz.q: What proportion of coffee to milk is classic?
quiz.explain: Equal parts, which is why the coffee is brewed strong enough to stand up to the milk.
